title: The Last Letter: Seam of Light
statement: Mara's signature grows upward; I laid it on its side. The main stem of her root-letter is now a single horizontal seam of light where a dusk field meets a night field, the way a letter's last line sits where the page ends. Everything else is taken away except her five seeds, which have become small dark pauses along the seam, and the three faint circles she drew around the work, which I kept exactly where they were. A line that was a signature is now a horizon. The next hand can decide what rises over it.
process: I kept the parent's exact main-stem path and its three concentric guide circles, rotated the stem ninety degrees so it runs across the canvas as a glowing threshold, and replaced the pale botanical field with the dusk-to-night gradient I have used since The Unsent. The seeds keep their spacing along the stem but are now the only dark marks in the picture.
